propositions: Prompt cache writes on every plan-review gate call and is never read across calls because the cache breakpoint is placed after pass-specific system prompt suffixes rather than at the byte-stable shared plan prefix boundary.

Single-turn plan-review passes (finder, verifier, prerequisite-verifier, coach, ticket-digest) each generate distinct system prompts with different cache keys, preventing cross-pass cache reuse within a single run despite sharing a byte-identical leading plan-prefix segment.

Same-ticket re-reviews within the 5-minute cache TTL would read a stable prefix if the breakpoint were repositioned to the shared_plan_prefix boundary, but this path rarely fires in practice because tickets are not re-reviewed within TTL.

The cache breakpoint can be repositioned from the end of the full system prompt to the end of the shared plan prefix by passing shared_plan_prefix as static system_prompt and the pass-specific stance suffix as a dynamic instruction, moving the cache control point without changing model-visible output.

Cache writes cost premium-rate billing (~9.2-9.5k tokens per leaf review) with zero benefit because each pass is single-turn with no intra-run reuse; a shared-prefix breakpoint would save ~5-6k token-equivalents per plan review through Pass-2 reads and TTL re-review hits.

The diagnostic warn_if_cache_ineffective only flags write==0 AND read==0, missing the write-every-call/never-read pattern; an aggregate detector must flag runs where cache_write>0 on every call but cache_read==0 across all calls.
